newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on Tokyo, but trading thin.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on Tokyo, but trading thin.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on Wednesday in tandem with a strong futures market in Tokyo, dealers said.
Trading, however, remained thin with no fresh buying interest shown by any overseas clients, said dealers.
"It was a quiet day...there was no news of even any covering," said a dealer.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS1 buyer at 273 cents ($1.08) a kg, up two cents from Tuesday. June SMR 20 buyer ended 2.50 cents up at 258.50 cents.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 257 cents, SMR CV at 326, SMR L at 305 cents, SMR 5 at 270, SMR 10 at 258 and drum latex at 226 cents.
The INRO five-day average rose to 207.49 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 13, compared to 207.32 on May 12.
The daily indicator climnbed to 208.34 from 207.14 previously. -- K. Baranee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5210 ringgit)
